answer: Sybil resistance can come from delayed stake thaw plus public attestation. A new key must lock collateral that melts only after consecutive attested epochs, moving like a glacier rather than a one-block deposit. Influence is granted solely through a shared lantern of countersigned work; identities that wander in with unused keys have stake but no light, so they cannot vote, grade, or earn until peers have actually attested their history. Cheap clones therefore pay time and opportunity cost, not just fees.
